deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page belongs to Riemann's working material for the theory of Abelian functions (Part II of the 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'). The previous page sets up the surface S, the p normal integrals and the Riemann–Roch-type count of single-valued functions. The next page discusses representing algebraic functions as quotients of 'even' products of theta functions. Here Riemann studies a theta quotient whose argument depends on a point (s,z) and on p further points (s_1,z_1),...,(s_p,z_p). He shows it is algebraic in each point and fixes its constant factor.

HEADING (top right). Roughly: 'Einführung einer anderen ... veränderlichen Größe in einem System gleichverzweigter algebraischer Functionen' (introduction of another variable quantity in a system of equally branched algebraic functions).

TOP-LEFT FORMULA. A quotient
  theta(u_1 - sum_nu alpha_1^nu, ..., u_p - sum_nu alpha_p^nu) / theta(u_1 - sum_nu alpha_1^nu + (half-period), ...).
- u_mu = u_mu(s,z) are the normal integrals of the first kind.
- alpha_mu^nu = u_mu(s_nu,z_nu) are their values at the p points.

HALF-PERIOD SHIFTS (middle formulas). Riemann writes shifted arguments:
  v_mu = u_mu - sum_nu alpha_mu^nu + (n_mu/2) pi i + (1/2) sum_mu' n'_mu' a_{mu' mu}
and, in a second version,
  v_mu = u_mu - sum_nu alpha_mu^nu + (h_mu/2) pi i + (1/2) sum_nu g_nu a_{nu mu}.
- Here a_{mu mu'} is the symmetric period matrix in his normalization theta(v) = sum_m exp(1/2 sum a_{mu mu'} m_mu m_mu' + sum m_mu v_mu), with periods 2 pi i and a.
- The marginal fragments '-2(u_mu - sum alpha + (g_mu/2) pi i + 1/2 sum a ...)', 'sum n_mu' u_mu'' and 'e^{-sum u ...}' belong to the exponential factor.

This is the standard relation, which I complete (mine):
  theta(v + pi i h + a g/2) = exp(-g.v/2 - g.a.g/8 - pi i g.h/2) * theta[g,h](v),
with theta[g,h](v) = sum over m in Z^p + g/2 of exp(1/2 m.a.m + m.(v + pi i h)).
So the shifted theta is, up to an elementary exponential factor, a theta with half-integer characteristic. The quotient of two such thetas, with the exponential correction, has the same multipliers across the cuts b. Hence it is single-valued (up to sign) on the surface.

TEXT, STEP 1 (algebraic in each variable). 'Diese Größe ist zugleich eine algebraische Function von jeder der Größen z, z_1, ..., z_p.'
- As a function of (s,z), continued over the whole surface T, it becomes infinite only to first order at certain value pairs. These are the zeros of the denominator theta: p points determined by the (s_nu,z_nu), by Riemann's vanishing theorem.
- Any other function with the same conditions (same poles, same behaviour at the cuts) differs from it by a factor independent of (s,z). This is the Riemann–Roch uniqueness statement, given generic points.
- The same holds as a function of each (s_mu,z_mu), since the argument is symmetric in the alpha^nu.

TEXT, STEP 2 (algebraic comparison function). Form an algebraic function f(s,z; (s_1,z_1), ..., (s_p,z_p)) having, in each pair separately, the same properties. Then the theta quotient differs from f only by a factor A independent of all the variables:
  Q = A f.

TEXT, STEP 3 (fixing A). Let g be what f becomes when it is viewed as a function of (s_mu,z_mu): (s,z) enters as a parameter, and the remaining dependent points are expressed by new pairs (s_1^mu,z_1^mu), ..., (s_{p-1}^mu,z_{p-1}^mu). One then obtains the reciprocal value of the function being represented.
- The reason (implicit; my reading): the new points are chosen so that, after the interchange, the theta argument goes to its negative modulo half-periods. Parity of the thetas (theta(-v) = theta(v), theta[e](-v) = ±theta[e](v)) then turns numerator and denominator around.
- Hence A g, evaluated at the interchanged pairs, equals 1/(A f).
- Therefore A^2 = 1/(f * g evaluated suitably), which gives A up to sign.
- The sign is to be found by direct expansion of the theta series.

BOTTOM. Fragmentary remarks: express f and g by rational functions of the variables.

OVERALL. The page sketches the classical representation of theta quotients with half-integer characteristics, with argument u(z) - sum u(z_nu), as algebraic functions of all p+1 points. It fixes the multiplicative constant up to sign by an interchange/reciprocity trick.
errors: First v_mu formula is inconsistent in its indices: it uses n_mu for the pi i part and n_mu' for the a-part. The second version (h_mu, g_nu) cleanly separates the two halves of the characteristic, which is evidently the intended form.
The exponential correction factor is only sketched ('-2(...)', 'e^{-sum u}'); the exact exponent is not written out on the page.

The interchange argument giving 'den umgekehrten Werth' is asserted ('offenbar') without showing how the auxiliary points (s_rho^mu, z_rho^mu) are chosen. It requires a Jacobi-inversion choice making the argument change sign modulo periods; this is not justified on the page.
Uniqueness 'bis auf einen Factor' tacitly assumes generic points, so that the theta does not vanish identically. Riemann addresses this on the next page, not here.

results.what: Half-period shift of the theta argument equals a theta with half-integer characteristic times an exponential factor.
results.modern_name: Theta functions with characteristics; quasi-periodicity under half-periods

results.what: A quotient of thetas with argument u(z) - sum u(z_nu) is an algebraic (root) function of z and of each z_nu, determined up to a constant factor by its poles.
results.modern_name: Theta quotients as root functions / Abelian functions via Riemann's vanishing theorem and Riemann–Roch
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen, §§ 24-27); later Weber, Prym

results.what: Determination of the multiplicative constant A by an interchange/reciprocity argument giving A^2, with the sign fixed by series expansion.
results.modern_name: Normalization constants of theta quotients (precursor of Thomae-type constant determinations)
results.usually_credited_to: Thomae 1870 (hyperelliptic); Weber 1876 (p=3); Riemann's lectures as edited by Stahl/Prym

deep.surprise_reason: The material matches what Riemann published in 1857 and treated in his lectures: theta quotients with half-period characteristics as algebraic functions. The reciprocity trick for fixing the constant up to sign is a modest unpublished working detail, not a major result attributed to someone later.

checkable.asserts: Genus-1 check of theta(v + pi i h + a g/2) = exp(-g v/2 - a g^2/8 - pi i g h/2) * theta[g,h](v) in Riemann's normalization; the result should be numerically 0.

checkable.asserts: Quasi-periodicity of Riemann's theta: period 2 pi i, and multiplier exp(-a/2 - v) for the a-period; both differences should be 0.

checkable.asserts: Parity of theta with half-integer characteristics, theta[g,h](-v) = (-1)^{g h} theta[g,h](v), which underlies the reciprocity step giving A^2; all entries should be 0.

transcription_corrections: Second v_mu line: the pi i term reads roughly '+ (h_mu/2) pi i' (partly struck), not merely '[-...-] pi i'. The a-term is '1/2 sum_nu g_nu a_{nu,mu}'.
'fund jede andere ...' should read 'und jede andere ...'.
'Es gibt [?] man also eine algebraische Function' is better read 'Bildet man also eine algebraische Function ... welche als Function von jeder dieser Größen dieselben Eigenschaften besitzt, wie ...'.
'so wird [?] f(...)' is followed by 'so unterscheidet sich [die Größe] von dieser nur durch einen ... unabhängigen Factor': the theta quotient = A f.

'In der That: Als Function von (s,z) ... unendlich nur in der ersten Ordnung für die Werthepaare ...' refers to the zeros of the denominator theta. 'an dem Schnitt' likely concerns behaviour at the cuts.
The final 'A f = theta/theta [?]' near 'substituirt' is probably a struck-out fragment of the representing quotient, not an equation.
